summary: The bill amends the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo and Alabama-Coushatta Indian Tribes of Texas Restoration Act to place those two tribes under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act by adding a rule of construction requiring IGRA's full applicability and repealing the two sections that created overlapping Texas regulatory restrictions.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends tribal gaming restoration acts to ensure uniform application of the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act. It contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, budgets, or expenditures. Therefore, it has no bearing on government spending.
The bill addresses regulatory jurisdiction over tribal gaming activities but makes no changes to tax law, rates, or collection. It has no relation to taxation.
No provisions in the bill concern healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services. The legislation is limited to gaming regulation.
The bill does not address firearms, gun ownership, or related regulations in any way.
The legislation pertains solely to tribal gaming jurisdiction and contains nothing related to immigration policy or border enforcement.
No content in the bill relates to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill makes no reference to military or defense spending or policy.
The legislation is silent on environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill does not modify any welfare programs or social safety net provisions.
No provisions address education funding, schools, or school choice.
The bill does not engage with drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
While gaming regulation can involve enforcement, the bill itself only harmonizes regulatory frameworks and does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No fiscal or debt-related measures are included in the legislation.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The legislation has no connection to foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No content concerns labor rights, unions, or employment regulations.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
